title: Pentaryn NPC Ties
description: Who knows who. Records directed relationships between actors — a stance, a one-word label, a strength and a page of notes — reads them on a Ties tab on the actor sheet — a reference panel of portraits, words and stances where clicking a row opens it to edit in place — adds them from the map with a key or the token HUD, and shows them on the canvas: hover a token and press the Ties key for a card per person that token knows who is in sight, or the step key for one card at a time through a crowded room with their token art, the word, their name and the notes. Drag a card to keep it; a thin line keeps it wired to whoever it is about. A third key shows a character's own written description instead — GM only. Players can use the tie keys on their own character — only their own connections, only what their token can actually see. Client-side apart from one relay: a player cannot write to an NPC, so their client asks a GM's to record the other half of a tie. A second tab, Known, is the character's own notebook: one entry per creature or person they have met, filed under Sentient or Beasts, with a page of prose in their own words — hover anyone you can see and press the notebook key to open their page, started for you if it is new. From a Known entry a player can ask what a creature actually is: a blind Study check thrown on the GM's own client, graded 15/20/25 into description, then what it shrugs off, then its real attacks — written straight into their notebook in the GM's authored words, which at low totals may be confidently wrong. One attempt per kind of creature, ever, with a GM reset as the release valve, and an optional hold so a good roll cues a scene instead of a paragraph. Exposes game.pentaryn.ties.
